name: giant crab

special_abilities.name: amphibious
special_abilities.desc: The crab can breathe air and water.

actions.name: claw
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 4 (1d6 + 1) bludgeoning damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 11). The crab has two claws, each of which can grapple only one target.

lore:
The *Decapodus Giganteus*, or the Common Giant Crab, haunts the jagged littoral zones where the surf meets the stone. These are not merely oversized scavengers; they are masters of the patient ambush. Often encrusted with living coral or kelp, they remain motionless for days, indistinguishable from a salt-stained boulder until a traveler steps within reach of their chitinous embrace.

Their predatory method is one of singular, crushing finality. Unlike the nimble hunters of the wood, the crab relies on a relentless, hydraulic grip. Once the primary pincer secures a limb, the creature retreats into the frothing tide, dragging its prize into the suffocating depths to be consumed at leisure.

Local mariners speak of the "Old Sunder-Shell," a legendary specimen said to be as large as a longboat. In coastal folklore, these behemoths are regarded as the silent jailers of the drowned, guarding the treasures of broken ships. To see one scuttling shoreward under a blood-red moon is considered a dire omen, signaling that the sea is hungry and the tide will soon demand a tithe of bone.
